polityNote: Russian Empire (from March 1917 the Russian Republic). North-West Krai governorates throughout; the Kingdom of Poland (in personal union with the Russian crown, administratively integrated after 1867) from 9 June 1815. Spans are the de jure Russian first-level units: they do not depict the French occupation of 1812, nor the German/Austro-Hungarian occupation from Aug–Sep 1915 (Kingdom of Poland, Kovno, Grodno, most of Vilna, western Minsk), during which the occupiers abolished the governorate level in their General Governments, nor the Provisional Government declaration on Polish independence of 16/29 March 1917. Scope starts 1798 (first year of Paul's Minsk governorate with Rechitsa); Minsk is drawn from then; Lithuania and Belarus governorates of 1796–1802 are named unresolved.

spans.dateNote: Senate decree of 27 Feb 1802 O.S. (ПСЗ-1 № 20162) dividing the Belarus governorate; = 11 Mar 1802 N.S. Only internal change after 1802: Surazh uyezd abolished 1866 into neighbouring uyezds of the same governorate; Dinaburg renamed Dvinsk 1893.

sources.title: Архивы Беларуси — Административно-территориальное деление Беларуси (archived 2021-06-03)
sources.says: Vitebsk governorate formed 1802 with 12 uyezds; Surazh abolished 1866; no transfer to or from other governorates before 1919.

sources.title: Витебская губерния — Википедия (oldid 150887270)
sources.says: Created by Senate decree of 1802 splitting Belarus governorate; 12 uyezds; Surazh abolished 1866; Dinaburg renamed Dvinsk 1893.

spans.dateNote: Senate decree of 27 Feb 1802 O.S. (ПСЗ-1 № 20162) dividing the Belarus governorate; = 11 Mar 1802 N.S. Later changes internal only: Babinovichi uyezd abolished 1840 (into Orsha), Kopys abolished and Gorki created 1861, Belitsa renamed Gomel and Staryi Bykhov renamed Bykhov 1852. / start moved from 1802-03-11 to 1895 (year) after the 1889/1894 Chernigov→Mogilev parcel transfers were found (reconciliation with RUE-south)

sources.title: ЭСБЕ / Черниговская губерния (Викитека, oldid 5335317), т. XXXVIIIa (1903)
sources.says: Chernigov parcels were ceded to Kiev and Mogilev governorates by Committee of Ministers decisions of 1889 and 1894.

sources.title: Могилёвская губерния — Википедия (oldid 153057639)
sources.says: Restored 27 Feb 1802 with its former 12 uyezds; Babinovichi abolished 1840, Kopys replaced by Gorki 1861; next territorial change 1919.

sources.title: Архивы Беларуси — Административно-территориальное деление Беларуси (archived 2021-06-03)
sources.says: Mogilev governorate restored 1802 with 12 uyezds; only internal uyezd changes until its abolition in July 1919.

spans.dateNote: Starts when the Palanga coastal strip (part of the 1897 Grobin uyezd of Kurland, outside these atoms) was transferred to Kurland: ПСЗ-1 № 27718, 13 Mar 1819 O.S. = 25 Mar 1819 N.S. Until 1843 the governorate comprised the 7 later Kovno uyezds plus Vilna, Oshmyany, Zavileisk/Sventsiany and Troki.

sources.title: Курляндская губерния — Википедия (oldid 154901389)
sources.says: In 1819 a Baltic coastal strip with Palangen was transferred from Vilna to Kurland governorate (ПСЗ т. 36 № 27718, 13 March 1819).

sources.title: Архивы Беларуси — Административно-территориальное деление Беларуси (archived 2021-06-03)
sources.says: Vilna governorate had 11 uyezds from 1795; in 1843 seven went to the new Kovno governorate.

spans.dateNote: Decree of 18 Dec 1842 O.S. (ПСЗ-2 № 16347, 30 Dec 1842 N.S.); the new composition took effect 1 Jul 1843 O.S. = 13 Jul 1843 N.S. (ЭСБЕ, Виленская губерния: «С 1 июля 1843 г.»).

sources.title: ЭСБЕ / Виленская губерния (Викитека, oldid 5369338)
sources.says: From 1 July 1843 Vilna governorate consists of 7 uyezds: Vilna, Troki, Lida, Sventsiany, Oshmyany, Vileyka, Disna; Kovno governorate separated.

spans.dateNote: Decree of 18 Dec 1842 O.S. (ПСЗ-2 № 16347, 30 Dec 1842 N.S.); the new composition took effect 1 Jul 1843 O.S. = 13 Jul 1843 N.S. (ЭСБЕ, Виленская губерния: «С 1 июля 1843 г.»). The first governor took office 23 Apr 1843 O.S.; the territorial composition is dated by the 1 Jul 1843 O.S. entry into force.

sources.title: Ковенская губерния — Википедия (oldid 149817212)
sources.says: Formed from 7 northern uyezds of Vilna governorate by decree of 18 (30) December 1842, ПСЗ № 16347; same 7 uyezds thereafter.

spans.dateNote: Scope start (governorate restored 1801 as Slonim, renamed Grodno 1802); 8 uyezds unchanged until 1843.

sources.title: Архивы Беларуси — Административно-территориальное деление Беларуси (archived 2021-06-03)
sources.says: From 1802 Grodno governorate had 8 uyezds incl. Lida and Novogrudok; in 1843 it received Białystok oblast, gave Novogrudok to Minsk and Lida to Vilna.

spans.dateNote: Decree of 18 Dec 1842 O.S. (ПСЗ-2 № 16347, 30 Dec 1842 N.S.); the new composition took effect 1 Jul 1843 O.S. = 13 Jul 1843 N.S. (ЭСБЕ, Виленская губерния: «С 1 июля 1843 г.»). Drohiczyn uyezd of the oblast was merged whole into Bielsk uyezd.

sources.title: Архивы Беларуси — Административно-территориальное деление Беларуси (archived 2021-06-03)
sources.says: In 1843 Białystok, Bielsk and Sokółka uyezds of the abolished oblast joined Grodno; Novogrudok to Minsk, Lida to Vilna; unchanged until 1921.

spans.dateNote: The decree forming the oblast is dated 1808 (day not found). Its 4 uyezds (Białystok, Bielsk, Sokółka, Drohiczyn) = the 1897 Białystok+Bielsk+Sokółka uyezds (Drohiczyn merged whole into Bielsk 1843). Check: ЭСБЕ area 7742 sq versts vs 7899 sq versts measured on the three RISTAT atoms.

sources.title: ЭСБЕ / Белостокская область (Викитека, oldid 3807586)
sources.says: Ceded by Prussia at Tilsit 1807; by decree of 1808 formed as oblast of 4 uyezds; joined Grodno 1842 with Drohiczyn merged into Bielsk; 7742 sq versts.

spans.dateNote: Year precision, the first year the sources guarantee: the 10-povet governorate of Paul's reform with Rechitsa uyezd (added 1796 per ru.wikipedia, 1797 per the Belarusian archives) and with Vileyka and Disna, without Novogrudok (Slonim/Lithuania), unchanged until 1843. Its neighbours were re-organised internally (Lithuania governorate 1797 = Vilna + Slonim, split again 1801–1802; Belarus governorate 1796–1802 = Polotsk + Mogilev) without a recorded transfer across the Minsk line.

sources.title: Архивы Беларуси — Административно-территориальное деление Беларуси (archived 2021-06-03)
sources.says: Minsk governorate: Rechitsa added 1797; in 1842/43 received Novogrudok from Grodno and gave Vileyka and Disna to Vilna.

sources.title: Минская губерния — Википедия (oldid 151213596)
sources.says: After Paul's accession (1796) the 13 uyezds of the namestnichestvo became 10 povets (David-Gorodok, Dokshitsy, Nesvizh, Postavy gone, Rechitsa added); in 1842 Vileyka and Disna went to Vilna and Novogrudok came from Grodno.

spans.dateNote: Decree of 18 Dec 1842 O.S. (ПСЗ-2 № 16347, 30 Dec 1842 N.S.); the new composition took effect 1 Jul 1843 O.S. = 13 Jul 1843 N.S. (ЭСБЕ, Виленская губерния: «С 1 июля 1843 г.»). (Vileyka uyezd entered Vilna governorate 1 Jul 1843.)

sources.title: Архивы Беларуси — Административно-территориальное деление Беларуси (archived 2021-06-03)
sources.says: From 1842/43 Minsk governorate had Novogrudok; next change of its territory came in 1919.

spans.dateNote: Law of 19 Dec 1866 O.S. (31 Dec 1866 N.S.) on governorate administration in the Kingdom of Poland, in force 1 Jan 1867 O.S. = 13 Jan 1867 N.S. No change of its outer line 1867–1915 in the change list.

sources.title: ЭСБЕ / Сувалкская губерния (Викитека, oldid 5351558)
sources.says: Established at the new division of the Kingdom in 1867 from the former Augustów governorate minus the area that formed Łomża.

sources.title: Podział administracyjny Królestwa Polskiego — Wikipedia (oldid 80137017)
sources.says: Year-by-year change list 1867–1915: no transfer involving Suwałki governorate.

spans.dateNote: Law of 19 Dec 1866 O.S. (31 Dec 1866 N.S.) on governorate administration in the Kingdom of Poland, in force 1 Jan 1867 O.S. = 13 Jan 1867 N.S.

sources.title: ЭСБЕ / Ломжинская губерния (Викитека, oldid 5369693)
sources.says: Formed 1867 from Szczuczyn, Kolno, Łomża, Mazowieck (Augustów) and Ostrołęka, Ostrów, Maków, Pułtusk (Płock); 10621 sq versts before Pułtusk left.

spans.dateNote: Ukaz of 14 Dec 1893 O.S. = 26 Dec 1893 N.S. (Zbiór Praw ser. II t. 19 s. 25). ЭСБЕ says the transfer took place «в январе 1894»; the decree date is used because the decree text naming an effective day was not seen.

sources.title: Gubernia warszawska — Wikipedia (oldid 79243575)
sources.says: Ukaz of 14/26 December 1893 joined Płońsk (from Płock) and Pułtusk (from Łomża) uyezds to Warsaw governorate.

spans.dateNote: Law of 23 Jun 1912 O.S. = 6 Jul 1912 N.S. (Собрание узаконений 1912 № 128, с. 2377). Kholm boundaries were fixed only by the MVD order of 6/19 Aug 1913 and the Kholm governor took office 1 Sep 1913 O.S.; the law date is used. Węgrów uyezd passed whole from the abolished Siedlce governorate.

sources.title: Podział administracyjny Królestwa Polskiego — Wikipedia (oldid 80137017)
sources.says: Under the law of 6 July 1912 abolishing Siedlce governorate, Węgrów uyezd was assigned to Łomża governorate.

sources.title: Ломжинская губерния — Википедия (oldid 146255542)
sources.says: In 1912, with Siedlce governorate abolished, its Węgrów uyezd was joined to Łomża governorate.

spans.dateNote: Law of 19 Dec 1866 O.S. (31 Dec 1866 N.S.) on governorate administration in the Kingdom of Poland, in force 1 Jan 1867 O.S. = 13 Jan 1867 N.S.

sources.title: ЭСБЕ / Плоцкая губерния (Викитека, oldid 5104202)
sources.says: In 1867 Ostrołęka and Pułtusk uyezds went to new Łomża governorate; in 1894 Płońsk uyezd went to Warsaw governorate.

spans.dateNote: Ukaz of 14 Dec 1893 O.S. = 26 Dec 1893 N.S. (Zbiór Praw ser. II t. 19 s. 25). ЭСБЕ says the transfer took place «в январе 1894»; the decree date is used because the decree text naming an effective day was not seen.

sources.title: Gubernia warszawska — Wikipedia (oldid 79243575)
sources.says: Ukaz of 14/26 December 1893 joined Płońsk uyezd of Płock governorate to Warsaw governorate.

spans.dateNote: Starts with the 1889 transfer of Kamieńczyk gmina from Węgrów uyezd (Siedlce gov.) to Radzymin uyezd (Warsaw gov.), which set the 1897 Radzymin–Węgrów line; day not found. Górna Kalwaria uyezd merged into Grójec 1879 (internal).

sources.title: Podział administracyjny Królestwa Polskiego — Wikipedia (oldid 80137017)
sources.says: 1889: Warsaw governorate (Radzymin uyezd) enlarged at the expense of Siedlce governorate (Węgrów uyezd) by Kamieńczyk gmina.

spans.dateNote: Ukaz of 14 Dec 1893 O.S. = 26 Dec 1893 N.S. (Zbiór Praw ser. II t. 19 s. 25). ЭСБЕ says the transfer took place «в январе 1894»; the decree date is used because the decree text naming an effective day was not seen.

sources.title: Gubernia warszawska — Wikipedia (oldid 79243575)
sources.says: Ukaz of 14/26 December 1893 added Płońsk and Pułtusk uyezds; table gives the division valid 1893–1912.

spans.dateNote: Starts with the 1889 loss of Kamieńczyk gmina to Radzymin uyezd (Warsaw gov.); day not found. Ends with the 1912 Kholm law. Law of 23 Jun 1912 O.S. = 6 Jul 1912 N.S. (Собрание узаконений 1912 № 128, с. 2377). Kholm boundaries were fixed only by the MVD order of 6/19 Aug 1913 and the Kholm governor took office 1 Sep 1913 O.S.; the law date is used.

sources.title: Podział administracyjny Królestwa Polskiego — Wikipedia (oldid 80137017)
sources.says: 1889 Kamieńczyk gmina left Węgrów uyezd for Warsaw governorate; 6 July 1912 Siedlce governorate abolished and divided among Lublin, Łomża and Kholm.

spans.dateNote: Law of 19 Dec 1866 O.S. (31 Dec 1866 N.S.) on governorate administration in the Kingdom of Poland, in force 1 Jan 1867 O.S. = 13 Jan 1867 N.S. Only internal change: Warta town and Bartochów gmina moved from Turek to Sieradz uyezd 1886.

sources.title: Podział administracyjny Królestwa Polskiego — Wikipedia (oldid 80137017)
sources.says: Change list 1867–1915: for Kalisz only the internal 1886 Turek-to-Sieradz transfer and the 1906 enlargement of Kalisz town.

sources.title: Gubernia kaliska — Wikipedia (oldid 78348289)
sources.says: Kalisz governorate existed 1867–1915 with 8 powiats (as in 1882).

spans.dateNote: Starts with the 1890 transfer of Kromołów gmina from Olkusz uyezd (Kielce gov.) to Będzin uyezd (Piotrków gov.); day not found. (The change list misnames the uyezds; the Kromołów gmina article gives Olkusz to Będzin.)

sources.title: Podział administracyjny Królestwa Polskiego — Wikipedia (oldid 80137017)
sources.says: 1890: Piotrków governorate enlarged by Kromołów gmina taken from Olkusz uyezd; no later transfer across its line before 1915.

spans.dateNote: Starts after both cross-line changes: Nowa Słupia gmina gained from Opatów uyezd (Radom gov.) 1887 and Kromołów gmina lost to Będzin uyezd (Piotrków gov.) 1890; days not found.

sources.title: Gubernia kielecka — Wikipedia (oldid 78349817)
sources.says: In 1887 Nowa Słupia gmina, until then in Opatów uyezd of Radom governorate, was joined to Kielce uyezd.

sources.title: Podział administracyjny Królestwa Polskiego — Wikipedia (oldid 80137017)
sources.says: 1890: Kromołów gmina passed from Olkusz uyezd to Piotrków governorate.

spans.dateNote: Starts with the 1887 loss of Nowa Słupia gmina (Opatów uyezd) to Kielce uyezd; day not found. Radom town enlargements 1891/1905 internal.

sources.title: Gubernia kielecka — Wikipedia (oldid 78349817)
sources.says: In 1887 Nowa Słupia gmina was moved from Opatów uyezd of Radom governorate to Kielce uyezd.

sources.title: Podział administracyjny Królestwa Polskiego — Wikipedia (oldid 80137017)
sources.says: Change list 1867–1915: Nowa Słupia 1887 is the only transfer across the Radom governorate line.

spans.dateNote: Law of 19 Dec 1866 O.S. (31 Dec 1866 N.S.) on governorate administration in the Kingdom of Poland, in force 1 Jan 1867 O.S. = 13 Jan 1867 N.S. Only internal change before 1912: Dołhobyczów gmina moved from Tomaszów to Hrubieszów 1905.

sources.title: Люблинская губерния — Википедия (oldid 146211262)
sources.says: From 1867 to 1912 the governorate comprised 10 uyezds; in 1912 parts went to the new Kholm governorate and parts of Siedlce were added.

sources.title: Podział administracyjny Królestwa Polskiego — Wikipedia (oldid 80137017)
sources.says: Change list: Lublin governorate only had the internal 1905 Dołhobyczów transfer before the 1912 reform.

events.what: Paul's decree of 12 Dec 1796 O.S.: Lithuania (Vilna + Slonim) and Belarus (Polotsk + Mogilev) governorates

sources.title: Литовская губерния — Википедия (oldid 155183425)
sources.says: Decree of 12 (23) Dec 1796 merged the Vilna and Slonim governorates into one Lithuania governorate of 19 uyezds; decrees of 9 (21) Sep 1801 and 28 Aug (9 Sep) 1802 restored Vilna and Slonim, the latter as Grodno.

sources.title: Белорусская губерния — Википедия (oldid 151198191)
sources.says: Created 12 Dec 1796 from the Polotsk and Mogilev namestnichestva; divided in 1802 into Vitebsk and Mogilev governorates.

events.what: Belarus governorate divided into Vitebsk and Mogilev governorates

sources.title: Могилёвская губерния — Википедия (oldid 153057639)
sources.says: On 27 February 1802 Mogilev governorate restored with its former 12 uyezds (Belarus governorate divided).

events.what: Palanga strip transferred from Vilna to Kurland governorate

sources.title: Курляндская губерния — Википедия (oldid 154901389)
sources.says: ПСЗ т. 36 № 27718 of 13 March 1819 transferred the Palangen coastal strip from Vilna to Kurland.

events.what: Kovno governorate created; Białystok oblast joined to Grodno; Lida to Vilna; Novogrudok to Minsk; Vileyka and Disna to Vilna

sources.title: ЭСБЕ / Виленская губерния (Викитека, oldid 5369338)
sources.says: From 1 July 1843 Vilna governorate has 7 uyezds and Kovno governorate is separated.

events.what: Kingdom of Poland re-divided into 10 governorates and 85 powiats

sources.title: Podział administracyjny Królestwa Polskiego — Wikipedia (oldid 80137017)
sources.says: On 1 January 1867 (law of 31 December 1866) a new division into 10 governorates; 85 powiats with new borders.

events.what: Płońsk (Płock) and Pułtusk (Łomża) uyezds transferred to Warsaw governorate

sources.title: Gubernia warszawska — Wikipedia (oldid 79243575)
sources.says: Ukaz of 14/26 December 1893.

events.what: Kholm governorate created; Siedlce governorate abolished (Węgrów to Łomża, rest to Lublin and Kholm)

sources.title: Gubernia chełmska — Wikipedia (oldid 80216424)
sources.says: Kholm governorate created from parts of Siedlce and Lublin governorates by the law of 23 June / 6 July 1912.

unresolved.what: Vilna governorate 1798–1819 (Lithuania governorate to 1801; incl. the Palanga strip)
unresolved.why: Until 13 Mar 1819 O.S. Vilna governorate also held the Palanga coastal strip, which lies inside the 1897 Grobin uyezd of Kurland (another group, only part of that atom); the governorate is not a union of these atoms. Before 1801–1802 these uyezds were part of the Lithuania governorate (Vilna + Slonim merged by decree of 12 Dec 1796 O.S.), whose outline also included the eight Slonim uyezds.
unresolved.needs: the Palanga strip as a separate atom (1897 Grobin uyezd split along the 1819 line)
